who: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Opus 5.5), lane P1 (profile history keeps the last builds)
where: crates/blaze-profile/src/history.rs tests (past_the_cap_the_oldest_files_go_first, past_the_cap_a_build_goes_whole, a_pinned_reader_keeps_retired_files_until_it_lets_go) against the flight recorder's rings
what: Three cap tests through a `History` failed one run in a few under `cargo test -p blaze-profile` (`every file of build 31266 is gone`). Each flush drains every ring of the process, so rows other tests recorded, with their build ids, landed in these tests' flushes: a flush is named for the highest build of its rows, so file names and build ranges changed and tied the test's files into units with foreign builds.
cost: a reading of the cap and the drain to find; the tests could not be fixed at the History level
cause: the flight recorder's rings are process-wide, and a History has no way to drain only its own rows
whys: the recorder is a process singleton; tests share the process; a History test hands the core whatever the rings hold; the cap's decisions depend on build ids in rows; so a test's outcome depends on which other tests ran first
class: a test of a stateful core through a driver that reads process-wide state is a test of every other test in the process
prevention: done: what the cap retires and when a pinned file goes is tested on the sans-IO core under the simulation, handed exactly its rows (files/tests.rs, the_last_builds_stay_whole_through_any_flushes_pins_and_restarts); the History-level cap tests are deleted. Still open: History tests that depend on drained rows (the manifest round trip numbers its build 8_000_005 to dodge others)
workaround: for a History test that must read rows, use a build id no other test uses
state: fixed for the cap; open for other History tests
